title: Clear cell acanthoma
aka: red dome papule on the leg
summary: An uncommon benign red, moist dome-shaped papule on the lower leg with a scaly collar. Dermoscopy shows dotted vessels in a ‘string of pearls’ pattern.

glance.think: A solitary, slow-growing, red-pink, moist dome with a collarette of scale on the shin of an older adult.
glance.engine: A benign epidermal tumour of pale glycogen-rich keratinocytes; possibly reactive.
glance.backbone: Dermoscopy; excision or curettage for diagnosis or symptoms.
glance.never_miss: Amelanotic melanoma, BCC, SCC and Bowen’s disease look similar, so biopsy if doubt.

what: A rare benign epidermal tumour (Degos acanthoma) made of pale, glycogen-rich keratinocytes. Some regard it as a reactive inflammatory dermatosis rather than a true neoplasm.
cause: Unknown. It often occurs on legs with venous stasis or chronic inflammation. Histology shows sharply demarcated psoriasiform acanthosis of PAS-positive pale cells, with neutrophils in the epidermis.
features: A solitary, slowly growing, **moist red-brown dome-shaped papule/nodule (5–20 mm)** on the **lower leg** of a middle-aged/older adult, often with a peripheral collarette of scale. It can bleed. Multiple forms are rare.
diagnosis: **Dermoscopy:** dotted/glomerular vessels in a **"string of pearls"** (necklace/reticular) arrangement. This is highly characteristic. Confirm with biopsy if there is doubt.
differentials: Amelanotic melanoma; Bowen's disease (glomerular vessels in clusters, not strings); psoriasis plaque; pyogenic granuloma; BCC; dermatofibroma; irritated SK; eccrine poroma.
management: Refer routinely to confirm (the differential includes amelanotic melanoma and Bowen's). Treatment (specialist/GP surgeon): excision, curettage, cryotherapy. Recurrence is uncommon.
red_flags: Pink lesion you cannot confidently name: refer, as **amelanotic melanoma** must be excluded.
pearls: A red, scaly leg papule that does not respond to emollient/steroid is not necessarily eczema or psoriasis. Look for a solitary lesion and **refer it for dermoscopy/biopsy** rather than escalating steroid potency.
